newsitem.title: USA: SEC acts in case of insider trading of Octel stock.
newsitem.headline: SEC acts in case of insider trading of Octel stock.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Wednesday it filed a complaint against a software engineer at Octel Communications Corp, alleging he engaged in illegal insider trading.

The SEC alleged Shahryar Soroosh engaged in insider trading in three separate brokerage accounts just before a company announcement last Thursday, which caused the price of Octel stock to lose more than 35 percent of its value the next day.
The commission alleged that Soroosh stood to profit more than $500,000 through the illegal trades.
Soroosh was not immediately available to comment.

The commission said it obtained an emergency order freezing Soroosh's assets in the three brokerage accounts pending a hearing on October 31 on the SEC's request for a temporary restraining order and other emergency relief.
On October 24, after the close of the market, Octel announced that a software upgrade would be delayed three to six months, the SEC said.
By the close of business on the day preceding the Octel announcement, Soroosh had sold short 35,000 common shares of Octel stock and purchased 80 put options, the SEC alleged.
The commission alleged that Soroosh knew about the delay of the software release when he engaged in the trades.
The SEC complaint also alleged that Soroosh's trading violated Octel's rules against employee trading five business days prior to earnings announcements.
The complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, seeks a permanent injunction against Soroosh, disgorgement and civil penalties.
